published_statement: Schwarzschild 1916 (physics/9912033) p.1: 'I have calculated the gravitational field of a homogeneous sphere of finite radius, which consists of incompressible fluid. The addition "of incompressible fluid" is necessary, since in the theory of relativity gravitation depends not only on the quantity of matter, but also on its energy'; eq (29) f4 = ((3cos chi_a - cos chi)/2)^2 (g_44 inside); eq (30) rho0 + p = rho0 * 2cos chi_a/(3cos chi_a - cos chi); eq (40) alpha/P_o = sin^2 chi_a; p.8 remark 2: 'with the small value thus resulting for chi_a and chi (< chi_a), all our equations coincide with the equations of Newton's theory apart from the known second order Einstein's effects'; remark 4: the light speed 'grows from the value 1/cos chi_a at the surface to the value 2/(3cos chi_a - 1) at the center'. Will 2014 (1403.7377) p.12: 'The iconic gravitational redshift experiment measures the frequency or wavelength shift Z = Delta nu/nu = -Delta lambda/lambda between two identical frequency standards (clocks) placed at rest at different heights in a static gravitational field ... The result is a shift Z = Delta U/c^2 (5), where Delta U is the difference in the Newtonian gravitational potential between the receiver and the emitter. If LPI is not valid, then ... Z = (1 + alpha) Delta U/c^2 (6)'. Klotz 2013 (1308.1342) eq (1): 'Under this approximation [uniform density rho], the force of gravity F_G acting on a test mass m at radial position r comes from the mass of the sphere below the object, due to the shell theorem: F_G(r) = -Gm(4/3 pi rho r^3)/r^2'.
published_hypotheses: Schwarzschild: constant density rho0 (homogeneous sphere), incompressible perfect fluid at rest with isotropic pressure p (eq 2), p = 0 at the surface
Schwarzschild: static, spherically symmetric; regular (finite, non-zero f4 and finite positive pressure) at the centre (fixes lambda = 0, sec. 5)
Schwarzschild: C^1 junction to the exterior mass-point solution at the surface
Schwarzschild: Newtonian agreement only for small chi_a (weak field), 'apart from the known second order Einstein's effects'; existence only for cos chi_a > 1/3 (R > 9/8 alpha)
Will: two identical clocks, both AT REST, in a STATIC gravitational field
Will: Einstein equivalence principle / local position invariance (alpha = 0); Z = Delta U/c^2 is first order in the potential
Will: U is the Newtonian potential sourced by rho (eq 30), zero at infinity
Klotz/Newton: uniform density, spherical symmetry, Newtonian gravity (shell theorem)

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (exit 0), 25 checks. N1: dsolve of (1/r^2)(r^2 Phi')' = 4 pi G rho, regular at 0, joined to -GM/r at R, gives Phi = -GM(3R^2 - r^2)/(2R^3) with Phi' continuous (derived, not assumed). N2: Phi(0) = -(3/2)GM/R = -2 pi G rho R^2; Phi(R)-Phi(0) = GM/(2R) = (2/3) pi G rho R^2. N3: ratio 3, crossover factor sqrt(3), exact in the Newtonian reading. N4: off-centre clock 2 pi G rho (R^2 - r^2/3); surface-vs-infinity crossover factor sqrt(3/2). G1: the full Einstein tensor computed from ds^2 = -((3sqrt(1-x) - sqrt(1-x r^2/R^2))/2)^2 dt^2 + dr^2/(1 - x r^2/R^2) + r^2 dOmega^2 equals 8 pi T for constant rho and Schwarzschild's eq (30) pressure (G^t_t, G^r_r, G^th_th residuals 0), p(R) = 0, A(R) = 1 - x; matches Schwarzschild eq (29). G2: 1 - sqrt(A(0)) = 3x/4 + 3x^2/16 + O(x^3), 1 - sqrt(A(0)/A(R)) = x/4 + 3x^2/16 + O(x^3): leading terms equal the tree's 2 pi G rho R^2/c^2 and GM/(2Rc^2); exact GR ratio = 3 sqrt(1 - x) (not 3). G3: at x = 1.33e-18 the crossover factor is sqrt(3)(1 - 3.3e-19); p_c/(rho c^2) = 3.3e-19. D1: tree uses CODATA G and exact c; G spread moves R* 2.8e-4 < 2e-3. K1 (side note): Klotz 1308.1342 printed eq (8)-(9), which use M(r)/r as the interior potential, give a centre speed 11.19 km/s for Earth, sqrt(2) above the 7.91 km/s that N1 gives and that Klotz's own text quotes ('near 8 km/s') -- a discrepancy in that restatement's printed equation, recorded only; it is not the source for anything used here and MUST NOT be quoted as an error in the journal version until that is read.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What the authors had: Newton's shell theorem (1687) needs only the inverse-square law; Schwarzschild (Feb 1916) had Einstein's Nov 1915 field equations and derived the exact interior with no empirical input beyond k^2 (G). The weak-field redshift Z = Delta U/c^2 (Einstein 1907/1911) rested on the equivalence principle, then untested. What came later: Pound-Rebka-Snider (1960-65, 1%), GPA (1976, 2e-4), Galileo satellites (2018, ~1e-5), and mm-cm-scale lab clocks (2022-23, 2207.07145) -- all confirm Z = Delta U/c^2; CODATA G inputs (1982-2019) spread 5.5e-4 but CODATA 2022 G is unchanged from 2018. Does it change the conclusion? No, evidence either way: (i) the coefficients 2 pi and (2/3) pi are pure mathematics given inverse-square gravity and uniform density -- no datum enters; (ii) the one datum, G, moves R* by at most 2.8e-4 across all 16 measurements; (iii) the only physics the Newtonian reading omits (pressure, O(x^2) GR terms, LPI violation) is computed here at 3.3e-19, 1e-18 and < 1e-5 relative. The regime the tree uses (cm, 1e-18) is exactly where 2207.07145 later measured the redshift gradient and found agreement within 1 sigma -- though in Earth's exterior field, not inside a source, so the interior-potential step remains a theorem (Poisson + shell theorem), not a measurement. Where M's suspicion has purchase here is not the outside math but the tree's prose: the unqualified 'EXACTLY sqrt(3)' is exact only in the Newtonian reading (GR: sqrt(3)(1-x)^(1/4)), and 'inside the region' should read 'at the centre'. Neither is a lack of data by the original authors.
grade_evidence: Statement: Phi(0) = -(3/2)GM/R = -2 pi G rho R^2, Phi(R) - Phi(0) = GM/(2R), ratio 3, crossover factor sqrt(3) -- derived here by sympy dsolve with regularity and C^1 matching (N1-N3), and recovered as the O(x) limit of Schwarzschild's exact 1916 interior, whose metric was checked against the full Einstein tensor (G1-G2). Redshift Delta Phi/c^2: READ in Will 2014 eq (5) and confirmed at the tree's own cm/1e-18 regime by 2207.07145. The hypotheses the canonical entry carries (uniform density, weak field, twin at infinity or surface) match the sources. Drifts in owner PROSE are recorded, each computed and none moving a number: weak field unwritten at excite.py:175-180 while 'EXACTLY sqrt(3)' is exact only for the Newtonian coefficients (GR ratio 3 sqrt(1-x); 3.3e-19 at the crossover); 'inside the region' where the value is the centre's (off-centre crossover up to sqrt(3/2) larger; S6's direction unchanged); LPI and pressure dropped (< 1e-5 and 3.3e-19). Data: G (CODATA 2022 = 2018) and c exact; G spread moves R* 2.8e-4 < 2e-3 tolerance. The crossover values themselves also depend on densities from address.py / Higgs results, which are not this result and are not graded here.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the tree's 'EXACTLY sqrt(3)' (excite.py:179-180) or '2 pi G rho R^2 inside the region' (excite.py:175-176) is used as a GR-exact or position-independent statement outside the weak field or off the centre -- e.g. applied to a compact source with GM/(Rc^2) not << 1, where the ratio is 3 sqrt(1 - 2GM/(Rc^2)) and existence needs R > (9/4)GM/c^2. DATA-DEPENDENT only if a future G determination moved by more than ~4e-3 relative (to shift R* past the 2e-3 selftest tolerance) -- no current measurement is within an order of magnitude of that. WRONG would need a failure of the inverse-square law or of LPI at the cm, 1e-18 scale at the level of the signal itself; 2207.07145 bounds the latter at alpha = 0.13 +/- 0.23 there, and nothing here shows either.
